The first PT_PROF sweep in _prof/ printed nothing because the profiling build never got to render: the Metal source failed to compile at startup.

What was wrong: my profiling patch guarded the mesh intersection with `if ((params.pad & 2u) == 0u && ...)`, but that code sits inside pt_intersect_scene, which has no local `params` — the parameters are reached through the scene struct. So newLibraryWithSource rejected the source with `program_source:615:10: error: use of undeclared identifier 'params'` and the program exited with 'metal init error: shader compile failed' before producing any benchmark line. My sweep loop hid that: it ran each invocation with 2>/dev/null and took `tail -1` of stdout, so every PT_PROF=... line came back blank instead of showing the compile error.

How I know it, and the fix: re-running one invocation with stderr visible (#54) showed the compile error; the function needed `scene.params->pad` instead of `params.pad` (#55-#56). After that single edit — no rebuild required, since the shaders are compiled at startup from the shaders directory — the same sweep produced the cost shares I recorded (#58): full 45.35ms, no shadow walk 44.05, no NEE 43.17, no mesh closest-hit 4.77, i.e. the BVH closest-hit walk is ~89% of the frame. The lesson I took from it is in my working memory: always check the base/candidate actually prints a benchmark line before trusting an A/B or profiling run, because the harness silently yields empty results when the runtime shader compile fails.

answer:
The first PT_PROF sweep printed nothing because the profiling build's shaders failed to compile at runtime, and my command hid the reason.

What happened, from the history:

1. In the scratch copy _prof/ I added four biased profiling shortcuts keyed off params.pad (bit0 skip shadow walk, bit1 skip mesh closest-hit, bit2 skip NEE, bit3 glass-always-reflect). The bit1 guard was written as `if ((params.pad & 2u) == 0u && pt_intersect_mesh(...))` inside pt_intersect_scene — but that function has no local `params`; it reaches the parameters through `scene.params`. So `params` was an undeclared identifier.

2. The host C++ build itself succeeded (the binary existed, and my grep-filtered build output showed nothing alarming), so the sweep ran. Because the program compiles its Metal sources at startup with newLibraryWithSource, the error only appeared then: `metal init error: shader compile failed: program_source:615:10: error: use of undeclared identifier 'params'`. The program exited before any frame, so there was no benchmark line to print.

3. My sweep loop piped each run through `2>/dev/null | tail -1`, which discarded stderr — where that error was written — and printed the last stdout line, which was empty. Hence six lines of `PT_PROF=n` with nothing after them.

How I know: message #52 shows the empty sweep; #53/#54 re-ran one variant with stderr visible and surfaced the exact compile error at program_source:615; #55/#56 fixed it to `scene.params->pad`; and #58 shows the same sweep working afterwards, giving the cost shares still in my working memory (gpu_ms_best: full 45.35, no shadow 44.05, no NEE 43.17, no mesh 4.77 → the closest-hit BVH walk is ~89% of the frame).

The lesson I applied later in the round: never trust an A/B base that prints no benchmark line, and always let shader-compile stderr through when a run comes back empty.
